html:
The heavy water sabotage was a series of attacks from 1942 to 1944 on the plant at Vemork in Norway that made heavy water, which Nazi Germany wanted for its nuclear research.

A British glider raid in 1942 ended in disaster. In February 1943 a team of Norwegian commandos trained in Britain climbed a gorge, slipped into the plant and blew up the heavy water cells without a shot fired. Later Allied bombing hit the plant, and in 1944 resisters sank the ferry carrying the last stocks across Lake Tinn.

Historians now think the German project was far from a bomb, but the raids were among the most famous of the resistance in Norway. They were filmed as The Heroes of Telemark. Compare the Allied Manhattan Project.
